newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan says about 30 countries likely to join ITA.
newsitem.headline: Japan says about 30 countries likely to join ITA.

text.p: About 30 countries are likely to express their intention to join a deal to scrap tariffs on information technology products before the end of the World Trade Organisation ministerial meeting here, a senior Japanese trade official told reporters on Thursday.

He said the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) was likely to cut tariffs in four stages starting from 1997 and finishing in the year 2000, but that there might be some flexibility about implementation timetables.

In addition to the EU, United States, Canada and Japan, many members of the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) as well as other newly industrialised economies and Oceanic countries were likely to join as well as non-EU European nations like Switzerland and Norway, the official said.
He said negotiators would meet in Geneva in January to work out details and there was a strong possibility of reaching an agreement on final content then.
He also said the Big Four trade powers had worked out most of their differences over the products to be covered by an ITA.
He said the United States was still resisting pressure to include optical fibres in the deal.
